column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. The curriculum addresses AI-assisted coding and developer workflows, Model Context Protocol and tool use APIs, requirements engineering and specification-driven development, iterative loop engineering, and system assessment. Students will be able to configure AI-assisted coding tools, construct agent skills and Model Context Protocol integrations, decompose requirements into executable specifications, analyse iterative loop engineering workflows, and assess AI-native software development systems. The course is taught through a combination of lectures, tutorials, and practical laboratory sessions involving hands-on coding and projects.

Course Code: Configure AI-assisted coding tools and developer workflows for a given software project, using agent orchestration frameworks, such that at least 80% of the provided acceptance tests pass.
column2: Construct agent skills and Model Context Protocol integrations for a given application codebase, utilizing specified tool use APIs, meeting the stated interface specification for every public method.
column3: Decompose requirements into executable specifications for a supplied software problem statement, covering every use case in the supplied requirements document.
column4: Analyse iterative loop engineering workflows and automated testing outputs, identifying at least three distinct failure causes with supporting log evidence from the execution trace.
column5: Assess an AI-native software development system for a complex multi-module project, justifying each design decision against at least one stated requirement and demonstrated live with scenario walkthroughs.
